steps.prompt: $97 \times 94$: both numbers are just under $100$. How far under is each one?

cards.title: Cross-subtract, then multiply the gaps
cards.body: For two numbers just below $100$, find each gap: $97$ is $3$ under, $94$ is $6$ under. Front part: take one gap from the other number, $97 - 6 = 91$ (or $94 - 3$). Back part: multiply the gaps, $3 \times 6 = 18$. So $97 \times 94 = 9118$.

steps.text: So $96 \times 98 = 9408$. The back part always has two digits for base $100$.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: $(100 - a)(100 - b) = 10000 - 100a - 100b + ab = 100(100 - a - b) + ab$. The front part $100 - a - b$ counts hundreds, and $ab$ fills the last two places. Above $100$ the gaps are added: $(100 + a)(100 + b) = 100(100 + a + b) + ab$.

prompts: Use $(100 - a)(100 - b) = 100(100 - a - b) + ab$ to explain why the back part has two digits.
